translationRepairs: Yin was still a child, so state affairs were in the hands of the senior ministers. Guo Wei, lately appointed chief of the privy council, had just crushed the three major rebellions and won towering credit—yet he and Min had old grievances. Min grew increasingly uneasy and asked his staff officer Zheng Qing, "The Son of Heaven is young, and power sits with the men at court. Guo and I have never been on good terms—how do you read the situation?"

Yin was still a child, so state affairs were in the hands of the senior ministers. Guo Wei, lately appointed chief of the privy council, had just crushed the three major rebellions and won towering credit—yet he and Min had old grievances. Min grew increasingly uneasy and asked his staff officer Zheng Gong, "The Son of Heaven is young, and power sits with the men at court. Guo and I have never been on good terms—how do you read the situation?"
判官鄭珙 names the aide 鄭珙; 珙 is Gong, so Zheng Qing is a wrong reading. The proposed Zheng Gong matches the Chinese and leaves the rest of the sentence intact.
Qing replied, "The Han regime is heading for chaos!
Gong replied, "The Han regime is heading for chaos!
珙曰 continues the same person as 鄭珙 in s0007; the short form must be Gong, not Qing. The replacement corrects only that name.
He told Zhao Hua, "Your counsel almost saved me—
He told Zhao Hua, "Not heeding your words, I nearly came to ruin.
不聽公言，幾至於敗 states that not heeding Zhao Hua nearly brought ruin; “Your counsel almost saved me” invents the opposite sense. The proposed wording restores the source meaning without adding content.
Chengjun said to Zhao Hua: "Had I listened to you, I would nearly have failed.
Chengjun said to Zhao Hua: "Not heeding your words, I nearly came to ruin.

The prior literal “Had I listened to you, I would nearly have failed” reverses 不聽 into a contrary-to-fact listen. “Not heeding your words, I nearly came to ruin” follows the Chinese negation and result.
Thereafter he prized scholars and installed the mountain man Guo Youwei in counsel.
Thereafter he prized scholars and installed the mountain man Guo Wuwei in counsel.
抱腹山人郭無為 is Guo Wuwei (無為 Wúwéi); Youwei misreads the given name. Guo Wuwei is the accurate English form.
